title: Publish is offered only for a goal with a landed commit
description:

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the `repository.publish` offer gate on `/affordances/read`. Nothing else.

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts:141-147 mints `offer(input, "repository.publish", publish:<goalId>)` for EVERY goal whose lifecycle is EXECUTION_ENABLED, CLOSING or COMPLETED - even with zero landed commits (seen live on UnAI 2026-09-04: a PUBLISH card over "No node of this goal is landed as a commit yet"). `offersForGoal` works from `PlanningOfferInput` facts and has no store; affordance-read.ts (:112 config.store, :263-266 composes the input) is where a landing fact is read.
- Landing facts: `readReviewLedgers(store, projectId, subjectRefs).landings` (apps/daemon/src/review/review-read-model.ts:287, :274-279) yields `LandingReceiptV1` per bare node key with `outcome: COMMITTED | REFUSED` (repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts:56-67); the goal's node keys come from its activated graph (the same walk the coverage read uses: document-coverage-read.ts readActive).
- SHARED FILES: goal-close child task-8145137ca3c144f0878deb83d05bab63 adds a readiness fact to the SAME two files (affordance-planning-offers.ts + affordance-read.ts). If that row is WORKING or REVIEW when this row is claimed, `moe.report_blocked` with blockedOnTaskIds = [task-8145137ca3c144f0878deb83d05bab63] and wait - never edit those files concurrently; when it has landed, ADD a second fact beside its readiness fact (same shape, one line in the ladder).
- Pinned consumers of the publish offer: affordance-planning-offers.test.ts:101-104 (expects ["goal.close","repository.publish"] once execution is enabled), affordance-read-planning.test.ts (goal.close/publish targets), affordance-read.test.ts:454/:498 offer roster, the board header's publish link (keys on the offer - memory board-screen-landed-2026-09-04), control-room goal-publish.tsx (renders on the offer), tests/e2e/control-room/board-chain.spec.ts (contract-less chain) - re-measure each and name every one the plan touches.

FEATURE: `repository.publish` is offered for a goal only when at least one node of that goal carries a landing receipt with outcome COMMITTED; a goal with landings all REFUSED, or none, gets no publish offer (the card then renders nothing - child 3). Contract-less/seed goals follow the same rule (a landing is a landing); the pinned fixtures that expect the offer right after activation are updated to land a commit first, each named.

=== THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE PLAN ===

FINDING 1 - THE PLAN'S FIXTURE NODE KEY IS WRONG. Probe over `openStore()` + `driveThrough(store,"goal.close")`:
  GOAL_LIFECYCLES {"goal-1":"EXECUTION_ENABLED"}

The seed world's activated graph names **node-a**, NOT node-1. The plan's step-2 positive arm (seed node-1 -> true) would have measured FALSE under a goal-scoped walk. Second probe confirms the working shape:
  LANDED_NODE_A a76b412a8b2c... ; GOAL_NODE_KEYS ["node-a"] ; LANDINGS [["node-a","COMMITTED"]]
So: positive arms seed **node-a**; **node-1** becomes the STRANGER key for the plan's goal-scope arm (4) - it is a real, landable node the goal's graph does not carry (LANDINGS [["node-1","COMMITTED"]] confirmed in probe 1), which is a stronger arm than the plan's invented "node-stranger".

Probe: `OFFERS_BEFORE ["goal.close@goal-1","repository.publish@publish:goal-1"]` with ZERO landing receipts - exactly the PUBLISH-card-over-nothing seen on UnAI. affordance-read.ts:247-248 EXCLUDES repository.publish from the bootstrap chain-offer path (only a STEP is minted there), so gating the ladder gates the whole surface. THE RULE AS BUILT. Node keys come from THIS goal's activated graph: `activeCompiledGraphs(store, projectId, LANDABLE_LIFECYCLES, ledger)` filtered by `graph.goalRef === goalId`, keys read exactly as document-coverage-read.ts:90-96 reads them (`content.snapshot.nodes` filtered by `executionBearing`, joined with `content.nodeAuthority.definitions[].nodeKey` — both rosters, because a landing attests a node's work and these are the only durable statements of which nodes are the goal's). `LANDABLE_LIFECYCLES` = {EXECUTION_ENABLED, CLOSING, COMPLETED}, the SAME set the ladder mints publish for. Zero keys -> false. Then `readReviewLedgers(store, projectId, nodeKeys).landings` -> true iff some receipt has `outcome === "COMMITTED"`. Whole body in a try/catch -> false: fail closed, an unreadable ledger is not evidence a commit exists. `folded` is threaded into `activeCompiledGraphs` so the surface's single fold is reused and no second fold happens.

NINE ARMS (deviations from the plan's six are recorded below and in comment-6d272018):
1. enabled goal, no landing -> false (the live UnAI defect, reproduced in a unit world).
2. absent -> present transition: false, then `seedReviewAcceptance("node-a")` + `seedLandingReceipt("node-a","COMMITTED")` -> true.
3. only landing REFUSED `{refusalCode:"NOTHING_TO_COMMIT"}` -> false.
4. COMMITTED landing on `node-1`, a node NO activated graph carries -> false, and the arm reads the receipt back independently (`nodeLanded(store,"node-1")` toBe "COMMITTED") so it cannot pass by the fixture having silently written nothing.
5. sibling-goal scope: same store, `goalHasLandedCommit(..., "goal-nobody")` -> false while GOAL_ID -> true.
6. before activation (`driveThrough(store,"approval.decide")` stops BEFORE it) -> false.
7. another projectId over the same store -> false.
8. fail closed: true, then `store.close()`, then `.not.toThrow()` AND -> false.
9. the caller's folded ledger passed in -> same answers (true for GOAL_ID, false for a sibling).

PLAN DEVIATION, forced (full evidence in comment-6d272018): **the plan's fixture node key `node-1` is not in the seed world's graph — the graph names `node-a`** (probe: `GRAPHS 1 [{"goalRef":"goal-1","snapshotNodes":[{"k":"node-a","bearing":true}],"defs":["node-a"]}]`). Seeding node-1 as the plan wrote it would have measured FALSE and the positive arm would have been vacuous. So positive arms use `node-a`, and `node-1` replaces the plan's invented `"node-stranger"` as arm 4's stranger — strictly better, because node-1 is a REAL landable node whose COMMITTED receipt the arm reads back, rather than a key with no receipt at all. Arms 5 and 7 are additions beyond the plan's six (sibling goal id, foreign project id); arm 9 is the folded-ledger contract the plan asked step 3 to rely on.
